_name: fu-compare - the follow-up A/B: every case run twice, NESSIE_FOLLOWUP_ROUTING=cc against =split
_why: The paid measurement of routing review section 5.6 (02-followup-loop FINDINGS section 7): 22 follow-up cases from the 2026-09-23 runs plus 3 new ones. Arm A runs with NESSIE_FOLLOWUP_ROUTING=cc (every follow-up to Container-CC, the 2026-09-23 rule), arm B with =split (the operator's 2026-09-24 rule). Same image, box and day; only the switch differs, so no case asserts a route (the manifest records the route each turn took) and no criterion reads Container-CC's trace or NExtSEEK's plumbing, which only one arm could produce. Every criterion is on the reply. Seeds run on NExtSEEK in both arms. Criteria fixes from FINDINGS section 7: refers-back turn 4 names HeLa and rejects 73; the CC mice follow-up rejects 1,442 and accepts only a subset of the 745; LUAD leads with 122; SHA expects 962 and rejects the invented 'first 20 rows'; NDMA seeds are keyed for fairdata-dev (207); no seed asserts api_ok. Case ids carry no usernames; each case's _why names its source run and turn, and questions are verbatim except one seed that named a person, reworded to 'the lab'.
_run: On fairdata-dev after rebuild 1 (rebuild the ns-sidecar too: the dev one had no aggregate op on 2026-09-23). Same image for both arms. Arm A: NESSIE_FOLLOWUP_ROUTING=cc in the app env, recreate the app container (then mkdir -p /app/runs and re-copy labs_db.json), and run manage.py nessie --tier full --cases /app/runs/fu-compare.json --pace 0 --user <account> --password-env <VAR> --out /app/runs/fu-compare-cc. Arm B: NESSIE_FOLLOWUP_ROUTING=split, recreate, same command with --out /app/runs/fu-compare-split. No --force-route in either arm (it would move the seeds too). --pace 0 is needed by ab.ns_chain_no_pause, the save-race case: the harness paces a whole run, not one case. PAID: 59 turns per arm, 34 after a seed; in arm A nearly all of those run on Container-CC (about $8-14 for the arm, routing review 5.6), in arm B only the controls, the table and what follows it.
_instance_warning:
NUMBERS ARE KEYED FOR FAIRDATA-DEV WHERE A DEV MEASUREMENT EXISTS (NDMA 207, the TCGA LUAD and MSI cases: 2026-09-23 dev suite; Kamm RNA 38, MIT_SRP 7,769, MIT_SRP liver 971, MIT_SRP NDMA 195: 2026-09-22 dev-box pin) and are production's (2026-09-23) everywhere else; each _measure entry says which. Re-pin every case on the box before the run:
  python NessieAI/tests/nessie_tests/scripts/pin_probe_truths.py --emit-cypher <this file>   (run the batch on the box, read-only)
  python ... pin_probe_truths.py --pin <this file> --from measured.json
Cases in mode 'each' list their numbers in the order of their locals.
Written by hand and not re-pinned: the reject-73 guard (ab.refers_back_to_the_newest_result turn 4), the reject guard for unfiltered counts (ab.cc_mice_transcriptomic), the leads-with-122 criterion (ab.luad_smokers), and the names (ENG, the assay titles, the TCGA study codes, HeLa, MUS); check them against the re-pinned numbers.

cypher: MATCH (s:T_MUS) RETURN count(s)
MATCH (s:T_MUS) RETURN substring(s.uuid,10,3) AS lab, count(*) AS n ORDER BY n DESC
MATCH (s:T_MUS) WHERE s.Genotype =~ '(?i)^CC[0-9].*' AND EXISTS { MATCH (s)<-[:DERIVED_FROM*1..12]-(x) WHERE x:T_A_GEX OR x:T_A_SCXP OR x:T_A_SPTX } RETURN count(s)
MATCH (s:T_MUS) WHERE s.Genotype =~ '(?i)^CC[0-9].*' AND EXISTS { MATCH (s)<-[:DERIVED_FROM*1..12]-(x:T_D_SEQ) } RETURN count(s)
MATCH (s:T_PAT)-[:IN_STUDY]->(:Study {title:'LUAD'})-[:IN_INVESTIGATION]->(:Investigation {title:'TCGA'}) RETURN count(DISTINCT s)
MATCH (s:T_PAT)-[:IN_STUDY]->(:Study {title:'LUAD'})-[:IN_INVESTIGATION]->(:Investigation {title:'TCGA'}) WITH DISTINCT s RETURN s.TobaccoSmokingStatus AS status, count(*) AS n ORDER BY n DESC

MATCH (s:T_PAT)-[:IN_STUDY]->(:Study {title:'LUAD'})-[:IN_INVESTIGATION]->(:Investigation {title:'TCGA'}) WITH DISTINCT s WHERE s.TobaccoSmokingStatus='Current Smoker' RETURN s.Sex AS sex, count(*) AS n ORDER BY n DESC
MATCH (s:T_A_ALN) WHERE s.MSIStatus='MSI' AND EXISTS { MATCH (s)-[:IN_STUDY]->(:Study)-[:IN_INVESTIGATION]->(:Investigation {title:'TCGA'}) } RETURN count(s)
MATCH (a:T_A_ALN {MSIStatus:'MSI'})-[:IN_STUDY]->(st:Study)-[:IN_INVESTIGATION]->(:Investigation {title:'TCGA'}) RETURN st.title AS study, count(DISTINCT a) AS n ORDER BY n DESC LIMIT 3
MATCH (s:Sample)-[:IN_PROJECT]->(p:Project) WHERE p.title='MIT_SRP' RETURN count(DISTINCT s)
MATCH (s:T_TIS)-[:IN_PROJECT]->(p:Project) WHERE p.title='MIT_SRP' AND toLower(trim(toString(s.Organ)))='liver' RETURN count(DISTINCT s)
MATCH (m:T_MUS)-[:IN_PROJECT]->(p:Project {title:'MIT_SRP'}) WITH DISTINCT m RETURN count(m)

MATCH (m:T_MUS)-[:IN_PROJECT]->(p:Project) WHERE p.title='MIT_SRP' AND any(v IN [m.Treatment1,m.Treatment2,m.Treatment3,m.Treatment4] WHERE v IS NOT NULL AND toLower(toString(v)) CONTAINS 'ndma') RETURN count(DISTINCT m)

MATCH (m:T_MUS)-[:IN_PROJECT]->(p:Project) WHERE p.title='MIT_SRP' AND any(v IN [m.Treatment1,m.Treatment2,m.Treatment3,m.Treatment4] WHERE v IS NOT NULL AND toLower(toString(v)) CONTAINS 'ndma') WITH DISTINCT m RETURN m.Sex AS sex, count(*) AS n ORDER BY n DESC
MATCH (s:T_PAT)-[:IN_STUDY]->(:Study {title:'LUAD'})-[:IN_INVESTIGATION]->(:Investigation {title:'TCGA'}) RETURN count(DISTINCT s)
MATCH (s:T_PAT)-[:IN_STUDY]->(:Study {title:'LUAD'})-[:IN_INVESTIGATION]->(:Investigation {title:'TCGA'}) WITH DISTINCT s RETURN s.TobaccoSmokingStatus AS status, count(*) AS n ORDER BY n DESC

MATCH (s:T_PAT)-[:IN_STUDY]->(:Study {title:'LUAD'})-[:IN_INVESTIGATION]->(:Investigation {title:'TCGA'}) WITH DISTINCT s WHERE s.TobaccoSmokingStatus='Current Smoker' RETURN s.Sex AS sex, count(*) AS n ORDER BY n DESC
